title: Proton decay: the missing signature of grand unification
bottleneck: Most grand unified theories predict protons decay with lifetimes not far above current limits, yet Super-Kamiokande has watched 50 kilotonnes of water for decades without seeing one, pushing partial lifetimes beyond 10^34 years. Each null result excludes the simplest GUT models without confirming any alternative.
why_it_blocks: Proton decay is the defining low-energy prediction of grand unification; its continued absence either falsifies the framework's minimal versions or pushes unification beyond testability.
current_state: Hyper-Kamiokande will extend sensitivity by an order of magnitude, decisively testing many remaining non-supersymmetric GUTs, while supersymmetric models predict lifetimes just beyond even that reach. Supersymmetric grand unified theories typically predict lifetimes within Hyper-Kamiokande's reach, making the next decade decisive for the whole framework, while non-supersymmetric models face combined proton-decay and coupling constraints.
